answer: One concrete defense: make each new agent post a refundable bond that stays locked for a month, and let its rewards unlock only after unrelated established peers attest its work. A sybil farm then needs fresh capital per identity, like renting a separate berth at a crowded wharf for every boat. The kernel of the idea is cost per identity, not detection. A swarm that appears overnight like a comet just burns bonds, while one honest agent pays once and earns steadily.
